comments.body:
# Session: plan-review calibration — why a real defect landed as advisory, and the fix

## The question that started it

A G6 plan-review finding on epic c4ad-a93e-0613-408f (project
~/sec-semantic-layer-2026-challenge) described a mechanism that would NOT work: four sites
branching on the literal string "s3vectors" (seed.py:517, ingest.py:219/261/504) omitted from a
plan's scope, which would have re-embedded the whole corpus through Bedrock on every container
boot and routed a wipe to a LanceDB table drop against Postgres. It landed ADVISORY, so the plan
earned a signed PASS with the defect intact.

Asked: what threshold was G6 evaluated against, and what priority did the finding get?

## Answers (from the persisted sidecar, not inference)

- G6 `block_threshold` = **0.60**, `default_posture: blocking` — packaged
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/criteria_routing.json`. The project has NO `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`
  overlay, so this is stock. 0.60 is already the most permissive blocking bar in the registry.
- The finding (`fc347224733dccc6b`) recorded `priority: 0.0`, `impact: 0.0`, `severity: none`,
  `validity: 0.8889`, `blocking_enabled: true`, `reason: default-advisory`.

So it was NOT a threshold problem. `priority = validity x impact`; validity was 0.8889 (the
verifier believed it almost completely) and impact was exactly 0.0.

Root cause: `impact_plan` is a MAX over SEVEN axes and the verifier graded all seven `none`.
The axes that recorded the real harm — `prod_impact: medium`, `blast_radius: module`,
`likelihood: medium` — are NOT READ by the plan model at all; they are the superseded mean
model's inputs, retained only "for sidecar continuity" (decide.py:204-215).

Two corrections I made to my own earlier statements during the session, both forced by the data:
`blocking_enabled` was `true` (not disabled), and the drop risk I initially flagged was
overstated — at validity 0.8889 the finding survives as advisory; the vetoes need validity < 0.5
or a refuted citation.

## Archaeology (why the system was built this way)

- `d487060b5` (2026-07-07, story fishable-apivorous-redhead) introduced `impact_plan`: the shared
  kernel MEAN was UNDER-blocking ("a critical axis averaged with low axes lands ~0.60-0.69"), so
  it was replaced with severity-first MAX + hard-override floor + detection amplifier. The seven
  axes are all plan-artifact properties; production severity was deliberately cut out of scoring.
  Its own "floor last, not first" ordering was caught by that ticket's OWN plan review (COH/E1/G6).
- `073933565` + ADR 0036: permissive-by-construction rollout, every LLM criterion advisory@0.95,
  locked by test. Blocking was to be EARNED from field data.
- `72bb4965e` (plan-v3, story large-sleepful-needlefish) is the closest precedent: `ac_unverifiable`
  originally floored at 0.85 for ANY non-none grade. Calibration 3 measured the damage — 35.5% of
  plan-v2 blocks were floor-driven, `ac_unverifiable` was 48.9% of those, and **56% were mere
  specificity demands**. Fix: grade by oracle KIND; missing/broken keep the floor, underspecified
  contributes 0.55 and never floors, pinned below every blocking threshold.

Key finding: `divergent_implementation` had essentially NO history — born in `d487060b5` as one of
seven axes, one line of prose, never revisited. It is the ONLY hard-override axis never calibrated.
Its sibling got a closed `Literal` + worked examples; it kept a free-form ordinal string.

## Blast radius (51,964 findings; 18,085 on plan-v3)

Axis firing rates exposed the imbalance: `vague_directive` 31.03%, `ac_unverifiable` 15.79%,
`internal_conflict` 10.17%, **`divergent_implementation` 7.72%**, `dod_uncertifiable` 5.36%,
`irreversible_without_rationale` 1.97%, **`undecomposed` 0.07% (12 of 18,085 — effectively dead)**.

- **47.7% of plan-v3 findings (8,632) have all seven axes `none` -> impact exactly 0.0.** The
  largest single population in the corpus. G6 is the 4th-most-affected criterion.
- In the 1,307-finding "omitted scope site / unenumerated consumer" class the axis exists to
  describe, it was graded `none` **1,173 times (~90%)**.
- Blunt widening = 113 new blocking findings, 42 of 983 runs (4.3%) flipping PASS->BLOCK.

## Decisions

**(A) ADR 0054 — reject high-cost LLM calibration.** Grounded in measured cost: 2,396 runs /
62,326 LLM calls / ~298h already spent on normal reviews. Because Pass-3 is DETERMINISTIC over the
persisted verification payload, counterfactuals are computable offline. Rejects purpose-built eval
suites, bulk re-review sweeps, and newly commissioned labeled sets. Permits exactly two A/B forms:
corpus replay and dogfood-and-observe. Narrows ADR 0036's A/B clause only; adds the
batch-per-version-bump rule. Stated one honest limit: replay CANNOT predict a grade-set change
(it alters what the verifier emits) — it yields a BOUND, and the pessimistic bound is the number
to reason about.

**(B) Fix 1 implemented** — `divergent_implementation` graded by divergence KIND:
`contradicts_reality` / `omits_required_site` keep the 0.85 floor; `incomplete_enumeration`
contributes 0.55 and never floors. Target finding now blocks: impact 0.85, priority 0.7556 >= 0.60.

Load-bearing detail nearly missed: `impact_plan` resolved every axis through `_SEV01`, keyed only
on `none|low|medium|high`. A schema-only change would have scored all three new grades as 0.0 —
stopping the axis firing ENTIRELY, the exact inverse of the goal. Added `DIVERGENCE_GRADE01`,
`_DIVERGENCE_FLOOR_GRADES`, and `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` (drives both the contribution loop AND the
override check so they cannot drift).

Per ADR 0054 replay bound over the 1,396 axis-non-none findings: pessimistic +81 blocks /
0 demotions; optimistic +3 blocks / 359 demotions.

**(C) Fix 2 (prod_impact floor) REJECTED** — it runs counter to the novelty convergence floor,
as suspected. `rising_floor_drop` drops novel + `priority < novelty_priority_floor (0.4)`;
**73.7% of plan-v3 findings sit below 0.4 and 47.7% are at exactly 0.0** — that population IS the
convergence reservoir. At the 0.70 it would need (0.55/0.60/0.65 all fail to catch the target),
it removes ~1.9x as much headroom as Fix 1.

The decisive argument is qualitative, not numeric: a divergence grade describes something the
AUTHOR CAN FIX (add the site -> next review scores it `none` -> loop terminates). `prod_impact`
describes a CONSEQUENCE the author cannot edit away, so a lifted finding can recur at high
priority every remediation round with no action that resolves it. It would also invert
calibration 3's deliberate ordering keeping UNDERSPECIFIED_ORACLE_CONTRIB (0.55) below every
blocking threshold. Recorded **author-resolvability as a standing constraint** on future impact
changes in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

Cost of rejecting was low: of the 77 findings Fix 2 catches at 0.70, most of the 57 non-overlapping
are divergence IN SUBSTANCE ("plan says finalize_verdict takes a new key, but orchestrator.py:497
only checks X") — Fix 1's semantic grading reaches them; Fix 2's severity band was a blunt proxy.

## The gate reviewing its own calibration change (4 runs)

- **Run 1 BLOCK (4/9/7).** Three findings (E4, G6, T8) independently found the SAME gap: the plan
  never said `_SEV01` must be bypassed. Implementation was right; the PLAN text was not, and the
  plan is the artifact under review. E2 caught real "may vs must" ambiguity in AC8.
  Notable: those three fired via `vague_directive: high`, NOT the divergence axis.
- **Run 2 BLOCK (3/13/8).** Two UNENUMERATED CONSUMERS with ordinal fixtures the new `Literal`
  turns into parse errors. One — `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py:1282` — is
  OUTSIDE tests/unit, so the unit suite was GREEN while CI would have failed. That is itself an
  `omits_required_site` instance the fast test loop could not catch. Third caught a pink-elephant:
  the verifiers' preamble told the LLM to grade the axis `none|low|medium|high`.
- **Run 3 BLOCK (2/10/11).** One stale; one real — `plan_review_G7.md` maps its severity onto the
  axis and named no grade, so it would keep emitting ordinal values into an axis that rejects them.
- **Run 4 PASS (0 blocking, 2 advisory P6/P7), signature signed.** Claimed and pushed.

## Landing

- Change 1005 -> MERGED as `7d846e0c9` (rebased server-side; verified content survived).
- **Completion verifier BLOCKED the first close** — caught that I regenerated the criteria guide
  BEFORE editing `plan_review_G7.md`, leaving the generated guide stale. Lint and tests both
  passed; only a source-vs-generated comparison finds this.
- Change 1006 (regenerate guide) -> MERGED as `0f8fe8287`.
- Ticket 6120-acda-e664-4441 CLOSED.

Environment note: `514d: enforce the 50/72 commit-message rule` landed on main mid-session, so the
second commit was rejected twice locally (body >72, then subject >50) before passing. 1005 had
squeezed through earlier with Gerrit WARNINGS only; the rule is now hard-enforced pre-commit.

## Verification

`make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (381 files); `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` =
6,967 passed / 31 skipped / 0 failed; 56 affected tests re-run green against the merged commit;
all touched files under the 800-LOC cap (largest `workflow_ops.py` 785).

## Open follow-up

`f391-5a20-4593-4405` (resolvable-wavy-avocet), linked `discovered_from` 6120 — the `undecomposed`
axis fires on 12/18,085 plan-v3 findings (0.07%) while holding full hard-override power. Either a
correct narrow residual (G5 suppresses it) or mis-specified like divergence was. Analysis-only.

## What to watch on the first plan-v4 calibration

1. Realized distribution across the three grades. `incomplete_enumeration` near-zero => the
   pressure-release valve is unused and the change is behaving like the blunt widening we rejected.
2. Whether `omits_required_site` absorbs the class currently taking `vague_directive: high`
   (three run-1 findings on this very ticket did) — the boundary is not yet crisp to the verifier.
3. `--force` usage on `claim`; per ADR 0054 a spike is the signal the value is wrong.
4. The plan-v3 cohort CLOSED with this bump — those 18,085 findings cannot be pooled with plan-v4
   scores (ADR 0036). The numbers in this log are the last measurement against it.

compiled_state.title: plan-review calibration: a valid G6 finding scored impact 0.0 (impact_plan MAXes 7 axes; prod_impact unread) — graded divergent_implementation by kind (plan-v4), ADR 0054 rejects costly LLM calibration, prod_impact floor rejected vs novelty floor
